questions.question: Recombination describes
options: generation of both parental and non- parental gene combinations
questions.explanation: Recombination is the primary method by which variation is introduced into populations in genetics. During meiosis, when genes from the mother and father reunite to form gametes (sex cells), recombination takes place. The exchange of genetic material between different organisms, also known as genetic reshuffling, results in the production of offspring with combinations of traits distinct from those of either parent. The process is genetic recombination. Hence the correct option is (B) i.e. generation of non-parental gene combinations. Recombination describes a generation of non- parental gene combinations.

questions.question: Mendel's law of Independent assortment can be violated by:
What did Alfred Sturtevant use the frequency of recombination between gene pairs to measure?
options: The distance between genes on the chromosome
questions.explanation: Alfred Sturtevant used the frequency of recombination between gene pairs as a measure of the distance between those genes on the chromosome, which helped in mapping their positions.

questions.question: Frequency of recombination between gene pairs on same chromosome as a measure of the distance between genes to map their position on chromosome, was used for the first time by:
questions.explanation: Alfred Sturtevant, a student of Thomas Hunt Morgan, was the first to use the frequency of recombination between gene pairs on the same chromosome as a measure of their genetic distance. He developed the first genetic linkage map in Drosophila melanogaster by analyzing recombination frequencies. The higher the recombination frequency, the farther apart the genes are on the chromosome. This work laid the foundation for genetic mapping.

questions.question: In Morgan’s experiments on linkage, the genes for white eye and miniature wing in Drosophila showed recombination per cent of:
questions.explanation: Morgan and his group found that even when genes were grouped on the same chromosome, some genes were very tightly linked (showed very low recombination) while others were loosely linked (showed higher recombination). For example he found that the genes white and yellow were very tightly linked and showed only 1.3 per cent recombination while white and miniature wing showed 37.2 per cent recombination.

questions.explanation: further apart two genes are on a chromosome, the higher the probability of crossing over (recombination) occurring between them. Conversely, genes that are closer together are less likely to recombine. Therefore, the distance between the genes and the percentage of recombination shows a direct relationship.
